cross_response_observations: The twenty-four responses cluster into several characteristic failure modes. Responses A, D, I, Q, and U rely on 'forced by elimination', 'forced by contradiction', or 'uniquely determined by permutation' assertions after one or two inspections, ignoring that the remaining envelopes form a derangement with a mixed envelope that can still share categories with the identified pure type. Responses F, H, J, L, M, S, and V commit invalid one-draw purity inferences, treating one observation per envelope as identifying its pure category and ignoring that a mixed envelope can return its majority on a single draw. Responses P and T derive their inspection counts from the minority count of seven (eight same-type observations exhaust the minority), missing that the worst case is thirteen majority observations from a mixed envelope. Response B leaves the synthesis hand-wavy without a concrete branch-by-branch rule. Responses E and N oscillate among incompatible counts (two, three, fourteen, fifteen) without committing to one coherent strategy. Response O substitutes an information-theoretic entropy calculation for any concrete inspection strategy. Response R correctly identifies the seven-thirteen asymmetry but miscalculates the same-type threshold as thirteen instead of fourteen, falling one inspection short. Response G achieves a structurally valid worst-case strategy but over-counts the total by one inspection. Response X refuses to commit any finite answer at all, citing a sampling-without-replacement objection inconsistent with the problem's stated twenty-sequence-per-envelope structure. Responses C, K, and W are the structurally closest valid attempts at fifteen inspections and fail only on the lower-bound impossibility argument: each derives why its specific strategy needs fifteen but stops short of proving no alternative strategy with fewer inspections can guarantee correct relabeling. The dominant defect category across the twenty-four responses is failure to engage with the worst-case branch in which a mixed envelope can mimic a pure envelope across enough observations to invalidate the proposed strategy.
